subject: Compliance packaging economics — audit logs, HSM choice, residency tiers & payment-term incentive
message_1_subject: Question on compliance packaging + pricing options
message_1_body:
Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looked great. Before we move to pilot, procurement asked for a clear breakdown of the compliance add-ons and how you price them. Specifically we need: 

- Line items and MSRPs for Audit Logs (retention tiers: 90 / 365 / 7y)
- KMS vs HSM pricing and estimated on-prem key-handling surcharge
- Data residency tiers (single-region vs geo-redundant) and per-GB egress implications
- Any HIPAA attestation or additional fees for covered entities

Also, can you outline any commercial levers for us on discounting (volume tiers, committed spend, or early payment incentives)? We have a procurement window and would like to compare total cost of ownership.

Appreciate a short written proposal we can share with our CFO/Legal.

Best,
Julia Park
Head of Infrastructure, AdeptRx
julia@adeptrx.com
Attachment: current_contract_outline.pdf (reference only)
message_2_subject: Re: Question on compliance packaging + pricing options
message_2_body:
Hi Julia — thanks for the clear list. I put together a short proposal and attached the detailed pricing table (compliance_pricing_v3.pdf) and a residency options sheet. Highlights below: 

- Audit logs: 3 retention tiers
  * 90d: $0.003 / GB / month
  * 365d: $0.008 / GB / month
  * 7y (archival): $0.015 / GB / month (cold storage)

- KMS vs HSM:
  * Managed KMS integration (cloud KMS): $0.00/month + $0.0015 / request
  * Dedicated HSM (bring-your-own-key or Redwood-managed HSM): one-time onboarding $12k + $2,500 / month for managed HSM per instance
  * Note: HSM cannot be bundled into the standard compliance discount — treated as an add-on (see Marissa's note below).

- Data residency tiers:
  * Single-region (customer-chosen): no base surcharge; cross-region failover available as paid add-on
  * Geo-redundant (active-passive): +12% on compliance baseline; + network egress per GB per region

- HIPAA: Redwood signs BAAs for any Dedicated or Private deployments. HIPAA attestation: included in the Compliance Plus tier for customers committing to 12+ months of reserved capacity.

Discount levers we can apply: commit-based tiering (3 levels), multi-product bundling (API + Dedicated + Compliance), and early-payment term (1% for net-10, 0.5% for net-30). For a first pass, we can offer AdeptRx a one-time early-payment incentive (2% credit on first 6 months) in lieu of stack discounts if you can commit to a 12-month reserved capacity (deal RDW-2026-ADEPT-78).

I copied Rishi and Marissa to confirm commercial treatment. If Ok, I'll send a clean quote and a DocuSign with the proposed payment-term incentive.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: compliance_pricing_v3.pdf; residency_options_sheet.xlsx
message_3_subject: Re: Question on compliance packaging + pricing options
message_3_body:
Neha — looks good. A few commercial notes from my side: 

- Pricing floor: for a startup-sized deal like AdeptRx (expected first-year usage ~12M tokens/month + 5TB of logs), I'd recommend the following committed tiers:
  * Bronze (12 months, $50k ARR minimum) — standard compliance pricing, no bundling credits
  * Silver (12 months, $150k ARR minimum) — 7.5% discount on compliance baseline + 1% EoP (early-on payment) credit for net-10
  * Gold (24 months, $350k ARR minimum) — 15% discount on compliance baseline + 2% EoP credit + one-time setup credit $10k toward HSM onboarding

- HSM treatment: strongly recommend Marissa's approach to keep HSM as separate add-on. HSM costs are lumpy and have hardware procurement lead time — including it in bundle discounts complicates margins and delivery. Offer a $10k onboarding credit only at Gold-level (to close the deal).

- Residency surcharge: instead of a flat +12%, propose a stepped surcharge tied to storage class and sync frequency (gives us flexibility on large clients). Will detail in the quote.

If Neha wants to offer a 2% credit as you proposed, lock it to a signed R12 (12-month reserved) and net-10 terms. I'll approve administratively for this account once the deal shows commitment in HubSpot.

-rishi
VP, Sales Operations
message_4_body:
All — quick pricing ops note:

- HSM: keep as explicitly excluded from percentage discounts. Offer onboarding credit only for mid/enterprise tiers.
- Audit logs: the long-retention (7y) pricing should require a minimum storage commit; add a $5k/year archival handling fee for small accounts to avoid negative unit economics.
- Early payment incentive: prefer a credit applied as an invoice line-item (rather than reducing list price) so it doesn't distort ARR comps.

If Neha goes with the 2% first-6-months credit as a sign-on incentive, we need a line in the quote that the credit is non-recurring and applied post-invoice, with a clause that it is revoked if the contract is canceled within 90 days.

Marissa Cole
Head of Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference
